issues.issue: Per-fund detail rule (cities and villages, 2026-10-27/28): when the only supplementary schedule is a combined all-funds one, detail is one line per individual fund column of the governmental funds statement AND the proprietary funds statement; combined-schedule lines are not used. p8 is that combined schedule. Fix: replace detail[33..36] with the p6 Water Fund and Sewer Fund column lines (utility cost-type categories, function utilities) and add their detail_totals. Milford_FY2024 already does this (Water/Sewer object lines).

issues.on_page: p4 Total Governmental Funds Taxes 1,036,251 (fund cells 889,133 + 71,200 + 50,228 + - + 25,690 = 1,036,251). p2 general receipts, re-read digit by digit: Property taxes 590,158; Property tax credit 32,499; Motor vehicle tax 51,490; Sales and use tax 305,966; In lieu tax 26,975; Occupation tax 29,162 = 1,036,250. p2 Charges for services 257,368 vs p4 257,367; both statements total 2,196,494.
issues.issue: Digits confirmed: the report itself is off by 1 between statements, with an offsetting +1 in charges for services (p2 vs p4), i.e. rounding shown in the report. Rule 4 of the tax-split evidence standard accepts rounding the report itself shows, so a p2-based split (incl. Property Tax Credit 32,499 as its own category) is arguably allowed; keeping it unsplit is defensible. Either way the 1-dollar cross-statement differences (taxes, charges for services) should be in report_discrepancies, which the JSON lacks (only in notes/review).
